01: [tense] It's August 1793, in Philadelphia, the capital of the United States. Your neighbor has a fever. Then chills. Then his skin turns yellow. [pause] Within days, he's dead. And he isn't the only one.
02: By September, the deaths climb every week. People stop shaking hands. Friends cross the street to avoid each other. People walk around holding rags soaked in vinegar to their noses, and the city stops ringing church bells for the dead. About twenty thousand people flee, and on September tenth, even President Washington leaves. [tense] Doctors bleed and purge the sick. Nobody knows what's causing it. [pause] The real killer is buzzing right past your ear. Mosquitoes. It will be a century before anyone proves it.
03: The city asks the Free African Society for help. Led by Richard Allen and Absalom Jones, its members nurse the sick and carry away the dead when almost no one else will. [calm] Then, in late fall, the frost comes. The mosquitoes die, and the fever stops. At least five thousand people were dead. About one in every ten people in the city. Would you have stayed, or fled?
